evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database analyzes oracle-bone and bronze 頁 as combining 卩 and 首, depicting a kneeling human with the head emphasized. It describes 頁 and 首 as graphic variants distinguished by whether the body is drawn, and reports oracle-bone examples for the head sense: 合集15684 豕頁 (“pig’s head”) and 合集22215 五子叩頁 (“the boys bow their heads”). Its shape account says oracle-bone forms may include or omit hair, a Western Zhou bronze form has hair, Warring States forms often distort the hair into 止, and the small-seal form omits it. It treats the paper measure use as a common form for 葉 and reports a change to 胡結切 by the Eastern Han at the latest. This is the database’s analysis, not a direct inspection of the ancient artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 字形、說文、廣韻、形義通解
evidence.text: The entry identifies 頁 as U+9801 and gives the Shuowen gloss 頭也 and 胡結切; it also lists Guangyun 胡結. Its analysis describes 頁 as head-plus-body pictography and cites oracle-bone contexts for the head sense. It cautions that the bronze phrase 頁手 appears only once and may be abbreviated or erroneous. It says 頁 and 首 were originally one graph and that the graph’s paper measure sense is a common form for 葉. The head-sense evidence and paper-use account are separate; the page does not establish the earliest dated instance of the latter.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：頁

evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 頁-seal.svg as a vector depiction of 頁 in Shuowen seal-script style, says the drawing was based on cited character-reference databases, and links to the original SVG. It reports that this digital representation is released to the public domain; the file is a modern drawing of a historical script form, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:頁-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The database’s legend states that its ancient forms are selected from the Xiaoxuetang databases and orders the represented forms as oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, then small seal; it also says the ancient-form sequence follows the referenced character books. The queried 頁 interface did not expose an individual record or glyph URL in the inspected page, so no Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.

evidence.text: Dossier-recorded account: the page reproduces the Shuowen entry and Duan Yucai’s textual-critical note, with oracle, bronze, Chu, seal, and clerical examples. The note disputes the received component wording; this is a later interpretation, not settled ancient graphic evidence.

evidence.source: Unicode Unihan data (official lookup attempted; supplied local dataset row)
evidence.text: The supplied local Unihan_Readings.txt rows give yè for 頁 (U+9801) and 页 (U+9875). The official Unicode character-specific pages were attempted during this run but were inaccessible through the browser, so these supplied rows cannot be represented as externally verified Unicode records. Both characters are distinct from any ancient sound evidence; neither is analyzed here as a phonetic component.

gaps: The earliest dated attestation of 頁 used for 葉’s page/sheet sense and a dated sequence of subsequent extensions were not established. The database calls this a common form for 葉, not a graphic development from the head pictograph.
The dataset’s reported Eastern Han latest bound for the 胡結切 reading concerns the head graph’s reading history and does not date the page/sheet usage.
The identity of the referents behind individual oracle-bone examples is reported through the database’s interpretation; no artifact image was independently inspected in this research.
The bronze phrase 頁手 is uncertain: the source considers abbreviation or error possible.
Duan Yucai’s challenge to the received Shuowen component wording is a textual-critical interpretation; the exact ancient formation cannot be settled from the received Shuowen gloss alone.
The official Unicode lookup pages for both U+9801 and U+9875 were inaccessible. The supplied local reading rows are recorded as local provenance only.
The Xiaoxuetang query did not yield a usable character-specific form image, and its precise official CC0 notice could not be opened in this pass; no image from that database is selected.
The second local Commons lead, File:Shuowen Seal Radical 324.svg, could not be accessed as an exact Commons description page, so it is not proposed.

items.period: Small seal script style represented in a modern vector drawing; the file page labels it Shuowen seal style.
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 頁 in Shuowen seal style. CUHK’s paleographic account describes small-seal 頁 as omitting the hair strokes found in some earlier forms.
items.alt: Black vector outline of the character 頁 in a seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Provides a clearly identified later form for comparison with the database’s account of earlier oracle and bronze shapes; source page states the precise style and gives the direct original file link.
items.rights: The Commons page identifies the vector as public domain and says attribution is appreciated but not required. The page also records historical courtesy/permission in its source metadata; retain the stated page terms for this specific file.

limitations.text: This asset is a modern vector drawing, not an ancient inscription photograph. Its seal-style label describes the form represented, not the date when the file was drawn.
No Xiaoxuetang form image is included: the inspected character query did not reveal a usable individual record or direct image URL, and no query-specific CC0 notice was verified in this run.
